config.title: Image Gallery

intro.title: Image Gallery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple image gallery component that displays a list of images. You will learn how to manage a list of data using React state and render it dynamically with the `map` function. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and JSX for structuring the UI. By the end, you'll have a working gallery that shows multiple images in a clean layout.
intro.usecase: Image galleries are a foundational UI pattern used across countless real-world applications. You'll implement them in e-commerce sites for product displays, in social media apps for user photo albums, and in content management dashboards for media libraries. As a developer, you'll build these components to handle user interaction—like selecting a main image from thumbnails—which requires managing state and events. Mastering this pattern is essential for creating intuitive, visually-driven interfaces that users expect in modern web and mobile apps.

objectives: Initialize and manage state for an image gallery using the useState hook
Implement a component that renders a grid of images from an array of data
Configure click handlers to update the gallery state when users interact with images
Apply conditional rendering to display a selected image in a larger view
Construct a functional image gallery with navigation controls (previous/next)
Integrate TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of image data
Manipulate array indices to control which image is currently displayed

steps.title: Define the image data type
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named `Image` with four properties: `id` (number), `src` (string — the image URL for ``), `alt` (string — short description for accessibility), and `title` (string — caption or tooltip text). Add this interface above your component so later steps can type the gallery data consistently.
steps.hint: Use the `interface` keyword. Match the shape the rest of this lesson uses: `src` and `alt` are what `` needs; do not use `url` here or step 4 will disagree with your interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: An Image interface is defined with the correct property types, enabling type-safe handling of image data in the gallery.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
